what: The hero video/photo plate that fills the screen is cut off at the top and sides while the next section rises, leaving only the bottom band as a rounded window: clip-path inset(0 0 0 round 0) → inset(77% 31.25% 0 round 10px) (below 768 wide: 90% 16%), and the inner plate zooms in 1 → 1.5×. This runs while the next section’s top edge passes from top 5% to top 50% of the screen (phone: top edge+300 at screen bottom → top edge+100 at screen top), with no curve and scrub 1

options.top · side: Top crop and side crop (%) of the strip to keep, default 77% · 31.25%
options.sp-top · sp-side: Below 768 width, trims the top and both sides, default 90% · 16%
options.zoom: Inner panel (data-fx-part=media) end scale, default 1.5 — at 1 it does not come closer
options.start · end: ScrollTrigger position based on the next section, default top-=5% top · top-=50% top
options.sp-start · sp-end: Position below width 768, default top+=300 bottom · top+=100 top
options.next: Next section css to use as the reference — if none, the nearest [data-fx-part=the next sibling of [track], or if there is none, the next sibling of the element
options.--fx-origin: Vertical position of the inner panel’s zoom axis, default 63.45% (phone 69.23%)
options.[data-fx-part=media]: 1 → inner panel (video or photo) that grows with zoom. If absent, crop only

use: Next section
note: The original sets the panel to sticky bottom:0 and lets the next section overlap it by rising 650px, so the cropped strip rises behind the next section’s text. That positioning is handled by the user’s css (see the use example).

from.where: index.html .rp-mv__clip (hero street video — original .js-home-mv-clip, relative to the next section .js-home-intro). The site build does the same thing in index.js
